title: Rookie Jackson Koivun holds off Scottie Scheffler to claim 3M Open, first PGA Tour win
content:
Barely a month after turning pro, Jackson Koivun fended off a charge from world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler and claimed his first PGA Tour victory with a final-round five-under 66 to win the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities in Blaine, Minn.

Koivun, who turned 21 on May 23, kept his cool as Scheffler applied the heat with eight birdies in his final-round 63. The former Auburn star finished with five birdies of his own to card a four-day score of 25-under 259 and best Scheffler by three strokes.

“I played a great round of golf today, definitely had some nerves coming down 18,” Koivun told CBS. “All throughout the crowd I kept hearing ‘Scottie’s coming, Scottie’s coming,’ and I just tried to tune that out and keep playing the golf I knew I could and was able to find some good putts down the stretch.”

The second-place finish was Scheffler’s fifth runner-up finish of the year. He began the day in a tie for ninth place, six shots behind Koivun.

Koivun shot a 10-under 61 in Saturday’s third round, including a record eight-under 28 on the back nine, to surge into the lead and enter Sunday with a three-shot advantage over Emiliano Grillo and Ben Kohles.

Hideki Matsuyama, Brian Harman, Chandler Phillips and Denny McCarthy finished in a four-way tie for third at 20-under 264.

Koivun turned pro on June 22 following the U.S. Open, in which he finished in a tie for 23rd with a five-over 285 at Shinnecock Hills.

The top-ranked amateur in the class of 2023, he signed with Auburn University. Koivun recorded one of the best freshman seasons in history, becoming the first college player to win all four major accolades — the Phil Mickelson (top freshman), Haskins (outstanding male NCAA Division I golfer), Ben Hogan (top male collegiate amateur) and Jack Nicklaus (national player of the year across multiple collegiate divisions) awards.

He repeated as winner of the Haskins, Hogan and Nicklaus awards this year and helped Auburn win its second NCAA team title in three years in June.

The 3M Open marked Koivun’s 13th career start on the PGA Tour but just his third as a professional. In his first dozen tournaments, he finished in the top 25 six times and in the top six three times.
